Set to one just before the sprite parking and room drawing calls at $1E18. The update at $4F9E checks and decrements it.

Saved Y for the bounded random helper, written at $0BD3 and restored at $0BE3.

Indexed coordinate limits shared by two platform step paths. $5E44 compares the selected byte against the incremented $95 coordinate and $5EBA compares it against the incremented $94 coordinate.

Title voice two writes the high nibble of the instrument pulse setting here at $1581 and to the SID low register at $1583.
Low nibble extracted from the same instrument setting at $1589 and written to the SID high register at $158B.

This span lies in the title player's initial $08 fill at $106D, which descends from $DC through $A3. Its later bytes include the two temporary fields at $C2 and $C3, written by the instrument-event code at $1638.

High byte of the source value stored by the third voice event path at $163E.

Remaining bytes of the first title instrument settings at $033C. The title driver reads $0341 at $1484 and copies it to its pulse-width state at $03A8.

The last eight $08 bytes after the third instrument settings, within the workspace initialized by the title player at $1065.

Identical to the same-address continuation of the title cassette bootstrap. Starting at $03D9 it programs the CIA1 timer latch, clears VIC IRQ and sprite enables, acknowledges the raster IRQ and returns at $03F0.

The title loader jumps here after loading tape record 490. The jump transfers control to $2D8C to reset the CPU stack and enter the resident program.

Clear $6E/$6F and the 26 zero-page bytes at $84. Choose three or four raster ticks from the value in $9813, generate all 256 bit reversals at $FCC0 and give the mission its initial two 16-bit counters.
X rolls through all 256 possible source bytes, and this branch repeats until it wraps. The unpatched screen-copy operands can appear to reference this address before their setup replaces them.

Prepare a new tower arrangement. Start with outer tower 7 and use $0BD1 to pick distinct room numbers for slots 1 through 3. Shuffle five entries at $0440, copy six candidates into the room records and derive two fields per room from the packed entries at $9AA6.

Set screen memory to $B800 in VIC bank $8000, write two lines of screen codes and scan the CIA keyboard matrix. Recognise the Y key as row mask $F7 with column value $FD and increment $9A4F to request a restored mission.
Twenty-one screen codes written to $B9C2 by $0A4A. This row asks whether to resume the saved game.
Twenty-one screen codes written to $BA12 beneath the first resume prompt row. The text shows the Y/N choice.

Build the tower arrangement, then use the saved-game path only when $A1D1 is zero. The cassette hand-over holds $01 there and skips that path. Initialize the raster display, load the tower resources and enter the elevator loop at $3A35.
Use the current tower at $86BA to select a one-bit mask and AND it with the flags at $A1D4.
Use the current tower at $86BA to select the mask ORed into $A1D4.

Sum the duration nibbles from $9AA6 indexed by six bytes of the active record. Reverse-copy 30 seed bytes from $A1D5 and call $0C17 for each of eight positions in the three slot groups. If $0B45 returns zero, add the three resulting counters to the tower counters at $9599. Pass the accumulated nibble sum to $0BE8.
Point the destination to $0440 and fill Y entries with A via $623F without modifying the fill value.
Generate a new byte via $3561, reduce it modulo the caller's accumulator value, return the remainder in A and restore X and Y.
Swap two randomly selected entries from $0440 for each iteration. A supplies the exclusive bound for both calls to $0BD1, and the outer repetition count begins at twelve.
A supplies a base offset. Add it to a random remainder below ten from $0BD1 and write the result at ($80),Y, advancing Y.

Preserve $9762 on the stack and switch off raster interrupts while the end sequence is prepared. Load three resources using tape table offsets $4B, $50 and $55, execute the overlay through its $7800–$780C jump table, then wait for fire.
Repeat the wait at $0C91 with Y counting down from 50, falling through into one final wait.
Take the current low raster line, decrement it and poll $D012 until that value appears. A caller can use this to wait for a raster wrap.
Compare the selected variant at $88E7 with the applied variant at $A191. If they differ, swap four pairs of 68-byte row groups and remember the new selection.

Set up the compiler frame for a 68-byte exchange between two caller-supplied pointers.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 8 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $0CFD.
Read the two pointers from the compiler frame. Swap one byte at a time and advance both pointers until 68 bytes have been exchanged.
Examine all six melody values. A zero entry returns zero early. Otherwise form the set of bits selected by the values and return one only when the mask equals $7E.

Increase $9808, derive the slot from the melody inventory state and write the value selected by tower index in $9A9E to $9809 plus that slot. Clamp the next slot value to five when the old slot reaches six. Convert it back to the state stored at $8DC3/$8DC4.

Save and clear the two panel state bytes, draw the active $9C63 rectangle and enter the panel controls after rendering the indexed fields. Redraw the inactive rectangle and restore the old state on return.
Set $7FD2 and write zero to columns $0C through $1A on row $18 through the mirrored character writer.

Initialize the panel via $2515, then draw mode-zero layouts from $9AE7, $9784, $9CAF and $9B21. Draw four numbered fields through $3577 with indices $12 through $15, place the tile from $9966 at column $0B and row $18, and continue at $1094.

Poll $344C until $0A releases $10, clear $7DF2 and latch the next input in $1D. Dispatch paired codes $14/$70, $12/$66, $13/$72 and $15/$73 to four drawing handlers. Return for $10, $74 or $0F. Clear the latch for other codes.
Compare the saved tile class at $1D with $14, $12, $13 and $15. Matching any leaves Z set.

Draw the selected panel, then skip its live view when the counter at $8DC3/$8DC4 reaches 150. Otherwise call $1130, set $7DF2 and poll $344C. On the repaint path draw columns $0D through $1A from the row buffer, print the counter via $1256 and derive the indicator tile from $9809, $7DF3 and $9967. On exit redraw the panel in mode zero.

Double the melody value from $9809 indexed by Y and add the low two bits of the incremented $7DF3. Index $9967 with the result and draw at column $0C, row $18. The exit at $0F42 silences the melody and clears the playback flag before redrawing the panel.
Draw the pressed version of the $9B21 rectangle. Read cursor and button state and call the panel-selection increment path while its carry permits repeating. Restore the unpressed rectangle on exit.
Draw the pressed $9C87 rectangle. Read the cursor and input continuously and use the decrement path while the button test and carry allow it. Restore the unpressed version on exit.
Four offsets spaced by ten bytes. The panel selection at $1C indexes the table. $0FDE and $0FF1 add the result to rectangle bases $9784 and $9CA5 for the two redraws.

When the 16-bit counter at $8DC3 is below 150, advance the selection at $1C modulo four and redraw the corresponding layouts from offsets at $0FC2. Increment the counter only with $7DF2 clear and call $1094 before returning carry clear. At 150 or above return with carry set.

Return carry set when the 16-bit counter at $8DC3/$8DC4 is zero. Otherwise decrement the selection at $1C modulo four, redraw two layouts using offsets from $0FC2, subtract one from the counter and call $1094. Return carry clear.

Draw the pressed $9C9B rectangle, update the cursor once and restore the unpressed rectangle. Continue polling while the cursor is over room-cell class $15, then clear the input latch and mirrored display row.
Repeatedly subtract ten from A until it is below ten, counting the subtractions in Y. Return the remainder in A.
Set the panel drawing colour, then divide the saved inventory word by ten repeatedly. Patch the three digit lookup operands with the remainders and draw the hundreds, tens and units on row $10.
Add the computed remainder at $9B33 to the glyph base low byte and carry into the patched page when necessary. The resulting tile is drawn at column $13 and row $10.
$10AF patches the low byte of the glyph source address with the remainder from division by ten plus $F5.
High byte of the first patched digit-table load. Initialize it to $99 and increment it if the low-byte lookup address crosses the page.
$10D6 patches the low byte of the tens glyph source address with the next decimal remainder plus $F5.
Page byte of the second glyph read. The address calculation initializes it to $99 and advances it on carry from the low-byte addition.
$10F3 patches the low byte of the hundreds glyph source address from the high decimal digit plus $F5.
High byte of the glyph-load operand at $10FB. Incremented on carry at $10F8 before drawing at column $11.
Multiply the AX word by the eight-bit step in Y. Test each bit of the step while shifting the input word and accumulate the result in A and $9B34, returning the high byte in X.
Set the selection timer to one, point zero-page address $5A at SID registers and write NOP at $1187 so the next melody call enters the player.
Replay the instrument's first seven bytes across the three SID voice blocks. Save each voice's gate pattern and copy four more settings into the SID global range.
Clear 25 consecutive SID registers and patch the melody entry at $1187 with RTS.
Runtime hook invoked by the scene raster handler. The opening floor snapshot holds RTS at this entry, and $2FDF preserves the first opcode while managing its wait state.
On expiration select an instrument and initialize it, then update the three voice patterns. Every sixteenth timer step advances $8DC3, which stops playback when it reaches $96.
Divide the elapsed count by 25 and index $9809 with the quotient. Copy the selected low and high instrument pointer bytes to $58/$59, then select three starting offsets and set their counters to one.

For each of three SID voices fetch the event-stream pointer and decrement its countdown. On zero read duration and note, advance that stream by two and write the indexed SID frequency. The count of one releases the gate.
Subtract the byte divisor in Y until the unsigned X:A dividend falls below zero. Return the remainder at $9B33 and the quotient at $9B34.
Read the first byte at ($30), zero-extend it at $1A and tail-call the division helper with divisor five.
For Y in rows $11 through $14, draw the two adjacent source tile bytes at columns X and X plus one. Advance the pointer $0A/$0B by two in every case.
Draw a melody tile pair at row Y and the next pair at Y plus one.
Three offsets spaced by 25 bytes. $12C8 adds them to $86BB to locate the melody slot selected by X.
Point $30/$31 at the 25-byte melody slot indexed by X, using the offsets at $12C5 and base $86BB.
Set the slot pointer and test its byte at offset one. If zero, discard this call's return address and return from the caller.
Screen columns 14, 18 and 22 for the three melody selections. $1312 selects the first column of a two-column clear. The four rows begin at 17 and the loop exits at row 21.
First melody entry index saved by $12FB for the redraw at $132C.
Second melody entry index saved by $130F and read back at $1356 when drawing the second row.
Check that the selected melody slot is populated before falling through into the two-row draw.

Load the draw-colour override from descriptor byte $18. Save two selection indices in $12E6 and $12E7 and clear four rows by two columns. Resolve each four-byte entry through the pointer at descriptor offsets $16–$17 and draw two rows per entry through $12BE.

Set the selection pointer through $12D7, then decrement its first field, wrapping zero through the value in its second field. Redraw two melody rows and update the selection through $159C, then call $335F twice and continue until the resulting selection reaches zero.

Find the active record through $12D7, advance its selection byte and wrap at five times the count in field one. Redraw through $12EB, divide the selection by five through $159C and call $335F twice. Repeat until the remainder is zero.
Selection record offset stored at $13FE and advanced at $1401. $141D restores it to Y for the next comparison.

Clear the match count at $9A3E. Visit three descriptors spaced $19 bytes apart, compare each populated descriptor's selected entry to its expected value through $16, and tally matches. Select the panel graphics according to whether any or all three match. The all-three path also calls $1B60 and $15B3.

After clearing the panel rectangle, draw the pair from $999F and $99A0 on rows $11–$14 at left columns $0C, $10, $14 and $18. Draw each populated melody selection through $12E8 and finish at the match indicators at $13F4.
Number derived from the current melody panel button at $14F4. It selects a ten-byte rectangle and is reloaded at $1516 to choose the next panel branch.

Wait for control code $11 to clear before polling panel choices. Codes $11, $70 and $0F exit. Map codes $09–$0E and $31–$36 to selectors one through six, draw the pressed graphic, call $1373 for selectors one and two or $13B0 with the selector reduced by three, then release the graphic and update the match indicators.
Save $A31C/$A31D into $7FA3/$7FA4 and clear both active bytes before the panel call.
Copy the saved bytes back to $A31C/$A31D and return zero in A and one in X.
Save the panel state and draw the active $9C6D rectangle. Display and handle the melody selections, then redraw the inactive rectangle and restore the previous state.
Working copy of X shared by arithmetic wrappers. The multiply wrapper saves it at $1584 and restores it at $158C. The divide wrapper saves it at $1590 and restores it at $1598.
Save X in $1583 and supply a zero high byte for the multiply at $2CA4. Restore the original X on return.
Save X in $1583, divide the indexed word through $2CD5 with a zero high byte of the divisor and restore the saved X.
Save X in $1583 and compute the signed remainder at the indexed word using a zero high byte for the divisor. Restore X on return.
Rotate an incoming carry of one into A at the tower's bit position. X counts down from the tower index.
OR the selected tower bit into the saved match flags at $877C.
AND the selected tower bit with the saved match flags and return the result.
Form the pointer $9599 plus three times the tower index in $16/$17.

Clear $9A3E and test the result from $15BD. When nonzero, find the source with $15C4 and copy its first three bytes, one into each record spaced $19 bytes apart from $86BB. Set the second field of each record to one. The zero branch clears both fields of all three records.
Enter the inline frame helper with a request for eight bytes of local workspace before choosing the tower backdrop record.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 8 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $161F.
Multiply the tower index at $86BA by 21. The record address starts at $8830 for variant 2 and $8836 for other variants.

Read a floor mask through $34. Bits 1 and 3 determine the first two row-group pointers through $32. Move the destination four bytes back and use bits 0 and 2 for two more pointers, then step back to the next floor mask and destination pair.

Fetch the current backdrop selection, apply variant swaps, and draw both strips of visible rows. Set up the current door and panel overlays, clear their scratch fields and finish by positioning the sprite through $2198.
Enter the inline frame helper with two bytes of local workspace before incrementing the vertical repeat counter.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 2 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $186B.
Run $18BF or $18B9 from bits 0 and 1 of the movement argument. Sample the returned bits again while calling the countdown update at $28C6 on each iteration.
Enter the shared movement routine with X equal to two and Y equal to one. This selects the subtract path for the elevator backdrop position.

Attempt to increment the scroll counter at $8DE2. Movement requires the counter plus fifteen to be below $9577. The shared entry at $18C3 also accepts the opposite direction from $18B9. Update the display and overlay before choosing the returned direction bits from the stick and position tests.

Split the scroll counter into a block from its high nibble and a reversed row index from its low nibble to fetch two row pointers. Patch $A18D–$A190 with those selections, draw the exposed left and right cells, then refresh the small overlays.
Seven little-endian pointers to the descriptors used for exposed backdrop rectangles, followed by a zero word.

Clear the screen via $35C5, then initialize the grid through $1E64. Fill 26 bytes at $8490 with one and draw successive mode-two panels from the script at $1A31. Complete the display through $1AFE, $23BA, $2183 and $2198 before calling $313A.
$1AC9 installs this list as the rectangle iterator's starting pointer. It supplies descriptors $892A, $894C and $8910, followed by the zero word that ends the loop.

Initialize through $35C5 and $1E64, fill 26 bytes at $8490 with one and fill the planes at $F000 and $D800 with $9570 and its lookup at $8BC2. Set the script pointer to $1A81, draw mode two while $20C1 returns nonzero, then call $1AFE and the subsequent room setup routines.
$1B17 reads the low byte of the first rectangle pointer. The room mode selects index zero or six.
$1B14 reads the high byte of the first rectangle pointer before calling the blitter.
Low byte of the second rectangle pointer selected at $1B53.
High byte of the second rectangle pointer selected at $1B50.
Low byte placed in $80 by $1B3D before the column writer steps through screen rows at stride 40.
High address byte paired with the low-byte array at $1AF6. The room panel code selects offset zero or six and places this byte in $81 before writing a screen column at stride 40.

Enable slot one via $3529 and handle scene modes one and six using the pointer words at $1AF2 or $1AF8. Draw the first panel in mode one. Draw the second in mode one if $9A3E is three and either $A1D1 is zero or the scene mode is six. Otherwise run $20AA with the third pointer and draw the second panel in mode zero. Finish through $3547.
When the tape-mode flag at $A1D1 is set, enter the animation only for backdrop variant six. With the flag clear, pass through to the variant selection.

Select the destination column and row-buffer pointer for backdrop variant one or six. Restore the pair of old tiles and draw the new pair on successive rows with a raster wait between passes. The loop also clears the corresponding bytes in the auxiliary map.
Alternate seven-entry pointer list for the room-edge redraw. The first four entries match $1A31 and the final three select other rectangle descriptors.
Register the zero-size frame before clearing the scene screen for the second room display setup.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 0 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $1C2E.

Initialize through $35C5 and $1E64, set $849C and $849D to one and point the panel script at $1C18. Draw mode two while $20C1 returns nonzero. Set the two panel pointers at $7FA9 to $958A and $95BB and finish through $2198 and $313A.

Select $31E3 or $3140 by $8DE1, clear $7FAE and pass the mode from $88E7 to the inline word dispatch at $1CF5. The handlers set the next scene mode and use $8DE2 to select the room entry path for modes one and three. The handler at $1C95 decrements the tower index modulo eight before loading the next scene.
Inline selector table consumed by $2DA8. Add -1 to the original selector, use one of the 6 indexed target words when in range, and select $1CF5 otherwise.
Select $31E3 if $8DE1 is set or $3140 otherwise. Clear $7FAE, copy display selector $88E7 to $0A and clear $0B before entering $1D9A.
Set $88E7 to two and enter the common display setup at $1DAF.
Set $88E7 to three. Use $1DC0 for room code $8DE2 of at least $10 and $1C28 for smaller codes. Return with X zero.
Set $88E7 to five, run $2A37 and enter common setup at $1DAF.
Set $88E7 to six. Use $1A89 for room code $8DE2 of at least $10 and $1A41 for smaller codes. Return with X zero.
On tape, leaving tower seven first runs $37E8, $31E3 and $599F. Advance $86BA modulo eight, choose display mode two, run $384A and enter $1DAF.
Inline selector table consumed by $2DA8. Add -1 to the original selector, use one of the 6 indexed target words when in range, and select $1D9A otherwise.
Clear the screen, redraw the tower panel and rebuild the elevator backdrop. Clear the map highlight flag before entering the shared marker restore path.
Register four local bytes before selecting the room raster mode and adjusting the backdrop coordinate.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 4 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $1DC6.

Decode the room index from $8DE2 and set up room data. Select entry coordinate $0168 or $00C8 by bit four of the room code and mirror the entry coordinates to $9764 and $97AC. Set the room parameters at $8CC2 and $7B, then initialize actors and draw the room.
Set bit five in the two current-tower record cells starting at A plus three and A plus nine. Save bit seven of the first changed cell in $8DC5.
Clear $258 bytes of the class grid from $82D1, fill the 40-byte strip at $8489 with class two and call $2EF2.

When the raster tick index is one, index $8489 with A and update the corresponding panel state. Flip $7FA7, advance $7FA8 on alternating eligible passes and use it to read the next value from the zero-terminated sequence at $8DF1.
Read X/Y byte pairs from the pointer at $30 until a zero X. Draw the same glyph in $32 at every pair through $3348 and advance the pointer by two each time.
If the highlight flag is set, branch to the glyph restore routine. Otherwise set the flag and draw the two highlighted glyphs at columns $13 and $14 of row four.
When $7FAE holds a column, restore one saved glyph on row four and three adjacent ones on row ten. Clear the saved column before rejoining the map path at $20A4.
Column calculated by the alignment path at $2011. It is copied to the displayed marker column at $2045 after restoring the previous tiles.

Derive a map-marker column from the input using the divide-then-multiply helper. Values below $13 go through the predecrement path and receive an extra increment. Save the computed column at $1FF2 and compare it with the old marker column before restoring old glyphs.

Save the first tile at $04A0, draw tiles through $3348 around the current column $7FAE and repeat around the second column read from $1FF2. Draw the neighboring tiles on row $0A, with the second group's upper tile on row four, then continue through $2083 and $20A4.
Divide and then multiply the word at $0E by three using the engine's arithmetic calls. Return its low byte in X.
If $7FAD is set, clear it and draw the saved tiles at $8DE7/$8DE8 on row four, columns $13 and $14. Rejoin the common return at $20A4.
Return zero in A and X and one in Y after updating the map markers.
Write A into the current cell and advance the pointer at $80 by 40, preserving A. Use X as the signed repeat counter for the column.
Read a little-endian pointer through $7E into X/Y, advance the source pointer by two and return the high byte in A as the list sentinel.
A second RTS byte immediately after the return from the rectangle pointer iterator.
Start the match at descriptor offset three. The CMP at $20DA covers the two-byte LDY immediate reached by the other entry at $20DB, and its flags are overwritten by the descriptor comparison.
Enter the shared check with Y set to one. Compare the descriptor byte with $20EC indexed by X. On a match decrement Y and compare the preceding byte against $20EB indexed by X.
Low bytes of the two descriptor signatures compared by $20E7.
Begins with the high byte used by X zero and continues with the overlapping low and high bytes for X one.

Choose the first panel data using the room code $8DE2, threshold four and flag $8DE4, drawing through $337F in mode two when that path supplies a panel. For the second, compare that room code against $9577 plus $ED and select the layout through $2159 or the default pointer $92EE. Skip the default draw when $8DE4 is nonzero.
Subtract the encoded room from three, scale it by eight and adjust a rectangle descriptor's pointer relative to $92AE.
Subtract the current encoded room from the position selected by $9577, scale the difference by eight and write the resulting pointer relative to $92CE into $A30C/$A30D.
Take the high nibble of the encoded room value, shift it right twice and add it to $8710. Return the resulting pointer in X/Y.
Store the two stream pointers $8BA5 and $8DC7 into the room-map state at $7FA9 through $7FAC.
Put eight times $88E7 plus $92 in sprite one's X register and $EB minus a quarter of $8DE2 in its Y register. Install VIC pointer $EE for its image.

Clear $8DC5. In display modes one and six require an agent frame below $0F and a coordinate at $8902 in $D8–$E7 before testing $0D54. Its nonzero path freezes the agent at frame $0F and loads the special room via record 128, then sets up the display and room pointers.

Run a delay before each pass over the tower screen. Copy groups of four tile bytes downward in screen memory from $F102 plus the group offset to $F0DA plus that offset. Clear four bytes at $F17A after each pass and repeat while the signed loop counter permits it.

Move layout index $88E8 up one except at index five, where it moves down one. Encode $0E as a room code with stride $20 and bias $11. Look up the group for $7FD4 and place $7FD5 into two fields before resolving the two tile selectors from $8107 onward. Convert the selectors to eight-byte offsets with biases $014C and $00AC before the room drawing calls.
Walk all objects counted by $80B2 at five-byte strides. If the search bit for an object is set, clear its countdown byte at $80B6 plus that record offset.

Five-byte records used by $37A2. The first word is a number rendered into three decimal filename characters; the second is the load destination. The fifth byte is present in the table but the cassette entry at $37A2 does not read it.
High byte of the little-endian file number in the five-byte tape request. $37AC loads it for the decimal digit conversion.
Destination low byte read by $37A2 and saved at $89 before entering the tape loader.
Destination page read at $37A7, followed by the requested length in units of 240 bytes.
One five-byte loader request. $399F patches its two-byte file number for the first room template group. The destination bytes select $A500.
Low byte of the second tower's file number. The computation starting at $2C2A stores the low part here after adding 130 to the group offset.
High byte paired with the second group's patched file number.
Low byte of the second tower load destination. It begins as $20 for $A520 and the write at $3851 clears it on the tower reinitialization path.

Five-byte tape requests following the opening tower requests. The file number occupies offsets zero and one and the destination occupies offsets two and three, as read at $37A2–$37B4. Offset four holds the length in 240-byte units and the $37A2 entry leaves it unread.
Minutes of the transition clock. $3F1F decrements them when the seconds subtraction borrows. If subtraction drives the minutes below zero, $3F24 restores the byte.
Seconds of the transition clock. $3F18 writes the subtraction result and the borrow path adds 60 before the common store at $3F33.
Transition clock expiry action byte written by $3F29. The initial value of its source immediate is six. $3F2E clears the immediate after that store.
The search reward path at $66AD increments this low byte after passing the reward index to $6881 to add a melody piece to the current selection record.
The search reward path at $66A2 increments this byte when control reaches $66A0 with carry clear, before subtracting nine from the reward value.
The panel transition at $21FC increments this byte before switching raster scenes. The tower update at $38FF also increments it when the flag test at $38FA returns zero.
Reward code seven takes the append call at $6698, then increments this counter at $669B and branches away when the increment produces a nonzero result.
High byte of the resident melody score, copied to $B36A for the weighted music tally.
Little-endian pointer to $37A2. The scoreboard copies it to $B36B and uses it to load assets while retaining the request index in X.
Second stored copy of the $37A2 pointer in the parameter record. The scoreboard copies it to $B36D before the callback at $B36F.
Little-endian pointer to $31DD. The scoreboard copies it to $B36F and dispatches through it before name entry to select raster lines $10 and $3A.
X value $37 for the scoreboard's first tape request, copied to $B371 and used at $A68A.
X value $3C for the second tape request, copied to $B372 and used at $A690.
Little-endian pointer to $2C98, copied to $B373. The scoreboard jumps through this pointer after its two restore requests.
Byte $01 copied to $B375 by the inline argument reader, between the continuation pointer and the saved-score import flag.
Byte copied to $B376. A nonzero value enables the scoreboard's $77 marker check before importing the saved table.
Byte before the pointer list used by the tower panel iterator at $2495. The mission-expiry path clears it at $2958 before jumping to the score overlay loader.
Five consecutive rectangle pointers used by the panel iterator. The first points to $97AE and a zero word follows the pointer to $8906.

Tile $0F for the descriptor at $97AE. After the iterator advances to $23A6, a read watch catches $24AB loading this byte at offset ten. $24AF passes it to the room cell rectangle fill. The second byte is zero and this loop steps over it.
Tile $10 for the descriptor at $9C63. VICE stopped after the load at $24AB with A equal to $10. The iterator steps by two, leaving the following zero byte outside the read.
Tile $11 for the descriptor at $9C6D. The read watch stopped immediately after $24AB loaded it from the advanced pointer $23AA plus ten. The following byte is zero and is skipped.
Tile zero for the descriptor at $A327. After advancing the list pointer to $23AC, the fill loop loads this byte via $24AB. The other byte in the pair is zero and is skipped.

Tile zero for the descriptor at $8906. The last successful lookup uses $23AE plus ten, confirmed by a read watch on $24AB. The next descriptor pointer is the zero sentinel, so the loop stops before another fill lookup.

Draw two forty-cell horizontal borders, then use the two selection loops to blit the tower panel pieces. Run the selected blit sequence through $20C1, store the timer descriptor at $A31C and draw the current tower's progress and time fields.
Save the return bytes temporarily, pull three argument bytes into $0E through $10 and discard a fourth byte. Restore the return slot and call $337F with the three arguments in X, Y and A.
Unpack the same stack layout as $24D9 and tail-call the room-cell filler at $3577 with the descriptor in X/Y and the fill class in A.
Compute the address for column $0B and row $10 in the room class grid and the companion display plane. Clear a 16-by-eight rectangle in both, advancing both pointers by $28 between rows.

Take the tower index in A. Draw the selected tower at row $11, its successor at row $16, and its predecessor at row $0C through $25EA, wrapping the indices at zero and seven. Select sprite pointer $EE for sprite 3 and write its position from $9751 and $9759 indexed by the selected tower.
Register six local bytes before drawing the row beginning at Y equal to nine.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 6 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $25F0.
Use the first argument to find a 21-byte tower record from $8828. Start at byte 8 of that record, set colour override 5 and begin drawing at screen row 17.
Draw A at column X and the map row in $32, then set X to zero for the next map record read.
Load the map row from $32 into Y and draw A at column X.
Fetch the column from tower record offset eleven and return it in A and X.
Register the zero-size frame before fetching the active tower's progress record.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 0 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $27F5.

Use the selected record's byte nine to set the displayed tower through $28A8 and $2558. Poll $344C until $0A differs from that byte plus one. Restore the tower display from $86BA and write the pointer $238C to $A31C/$A31D.
Multiply the word drawn from $11 and X by $15 and add $8828. Store the resulting pointer in $A31C/$A31D.
Read the rectangle index from offset nine of the record pointer at $06. Multiply it by ten and add $A334, returning the descriptor pointer in X/Y.
One shared sprite multicolour value per tower. $28BC copies the selected colour to $D025 while updating the marker.
One sprite colour per tower. $28C2 writes the selected colour to sprite two.
Use the tower number to set sprite two's pointer to $F7 plus the index, put it at $50/$B4 and select its shared and individual colours from the two adjacent tables.

Subtract the current frame-rate threshold $9813 from elapsed ticks at $4C. After reaching the threshold update the current tower clock and the mission clock, then draw the three displayed time bytes through the pointer at $A31C when the elevator panel is active.
Run the screen transition, clear $23A3 and jump to the loader for the score program.

Subtract one from the seconds field. Signed underflow writes back 59, borrows from minutes and performs the same wrap before decrementing hours. The low-time path checks the other two fields before calling the warning routine.
Set voice one's frequency high byte and envelope, then write the triangle waveform control first without and then with its gate bit.
Set voice one's frequency high byte to four and write its envelope. Clear the voice-two and voice-three controls, then write voice one's noise waveform first without and then with the gate bit.
Convert A through $99F5, set row $10 and pass the resulting character and the caller's X column to the screen writer at $3348.
Subtract one from the byte selected by Y in the three-byte record pointed to by $30 and store it back without altering Y.
Divide A by ten and return the quotient in A. Keep the remainder in $32 for the following units-digit draw.
Multiply outer tower number by the 21-byte record stride and add the base $8828, returning the resulting address in X:Y.
Multiply the outer tower number by ten, add $A334 and return the record address in X:Y.
Return zero in A and X and the constant one in Y.
Return immediately for raster scene zero. Otherwise initialize the actors at $7D26 before falling through to the room pack path.
Prepare the record pointers for the room number at $88E8 and jump to the packer.
Save the new room number at $88E8, prepare its pointers and jump to the resident room unpacker.
Multiply the room slot by $01A9 and add $B400 for the saved room record. Return that address in $0E/$0F and seed the decode destination at $7FD3 in $12/$13.
Register two local bytes before initializing the HUD sprite and checking the panel selection.
Three-byte descriptor consumed by $2DE8. Save 2 working bytes from $30, then apply the following zero stack adjustment and enter $2A7F.
Refresh sprite state, set the enable mask from $A192 and store two input parameters at $893A. Wait for selection $0F to clear before polling again and dispatching through $2B19.
Inline selector table consumed by $2DA8. Add -1 to the original selector, use one of the 17 indexed target words when in range, and select $2B44 otherwise.
Tail-jump to $2A9E. The decoder at $2B48 has a separate entry.
A $60 byte between the unconditional tail jump at $2B44 and the separate packer entry at $2B48. The jump bypasses this byte.

Read three groups of $FE source bytes through $12/$13. Choose a zero-through-three length class from each byte's magnitude, then emit the class and that many two-bit groups through $2BA9. Finish by calling $2BA9 three times to move the last bits through the accumulator.
Shift two high bits from A into $17 and keep the shifted accumulator. After the fourth call of a group, store the assembled byte through $0E and advance the 16-bit destination pointer.
Read the compressed data through $0E/$0F and write successive decoded bytes through $12/$13. The nested counters run for three groups of 254 bytes, filling $7FD3–$82CC at the normal destination.
Take the first two bits from the compressed stream as a count of base-four digits. Zero yields zero directly. Otherwise consume that many additional two-bit digits and return them combined in A.
When the bit-pair counter is empty, load a new source byte into $16 and advance the source pointer. Count off one of the four pairs; the caller shifts the high pair out.
Convert outer tower number to the file name base by multiplying by 16 and adding 130, store the two-byte result at $233C and load the resource entry at index $0A.
Double the supplied room number into the low file number byte at $2332 and dispatch through the loader table's first slot.
Locate the destination record through $2A52 and copy $01A9 bytes from the returned X:Y address using $6217. Finish through the room decoder at $2BCA.
Select a display cleanup according to $8DE1, blank VIC output and call the loader with table offset $41. Set $0291 to $80 and call the overlay's entry at $A520.
Last index $17 for the descending parameter copy at $A679. This copies 24 bytes including index zero.
Little-endian pointer to the parameter block at $238C. The scoreboard loads its two bytes at $A66C and $A671.
First resource index passed to the tape callback after the scoreboard. The score overlay copies it at $A661 and passes it in X at $A6F0.
Second resource index passed to the tape callback after the scoreboard. The overlay copies it at $A667 and passes it in X at $A712.
Set the transition flag at $A1F3 and run $6A76, then reload tape block 490 with interrupts disabled. Run the loader's $BFFD tail and jump to the original game entry.

Multiply the word at zero-page index Y by the word in A and X. Rotate the partial product and the indexed word 16 times, conditionally adding the saved factor when the next multiplier bit is one. Return the lower product at the indexed word and leave the upper part at $02/$03.
Use the signed division setup at $2D3E. If the dividend and divisor had different signs, negate the quotient stored in the indexed word. Return with X zero and Y one.
Divide through $2D3E and copy the remainder from $02/$03 back to the indexed word. Give the remainder the original dividend's sign using the saved byte at $27.
Call the unsigned setup entry at $2D10 and then store $02/$03 back to the indexed word. A controlled entry with dividend 43 and divisor three returned one at the writeback.
Save the divisor from AX at $24/$25, copy the dividend offset Y to X, zero Y and enter the shift-and-subtract routine.
With X selecting the dividend and $24/$25 containing the divisor, shift 16 dividend bits into $02/$03. Subtract the divisor when it fits and set the quotient bit in the low dividend byte.

Save AX in $24/$25 and move the dividend's zero-page offset from Y into X. Save the dividend sign and the XOR of both signs, take the magnitude of each negative input and jump into the 16-step divider.
Shift the word at zero-page index Y left by the count in A, rotating each carry into its high byte. The outer counter in X controls any further 256-shift groups. Return with A and X zero and Y one.
Clear decimal mode, bank I/O in with both ROMs out, pull the top two stack bytes into $88E5/$88E6, reset the software stack pointer to $023F and hardware stack to $FF, then jump to $0AD4.

Pull a pointer to the bytes following the call. Add the first inline word to $0A/$0B and compare against the second. For an in-range selector index the inline target table by twice the adjusted value; otherwise use the default pointer. Jump indirectly through $0A.

Pull the address of the inline frame descriptor, save $04–$09 on the hardware stack and copy the specified number of work bytes from $30 into the software stack. Synthetic return address $2E57 causes the inline routine's RTS to enter the restoration code.

Restore the working zero-page prefix from the frame if its saved length is nonzero. Restore pointers $04–$09, retrieve the original call site, drop the number of stack bytes specified by its inline descriptor and jump to the caller's continuation.
Disable VIC interrupt sources at $D01A, then read and write back IRQ status at $D019 to acknowledge the flags already set.

Configure the VIC interrupt source, select VIC bank $C000 by clearing CIA2 port A bits 0–1 and enable multicolour characters. Schedule the first raster event and install hardware IRQ $2F86 and NMI $2ED8.
Preserve A, X and Y, select I/O-visible RAM banking and restore the common RTI opcode from $2FBD at the NMI entry before transferring to $3012.
Preserve A and set $8DE1 to 3. The IRQ scheduler uses this value as the raster table index on wrap.
Preserve A and clear $8DE1. The IRQ scheduler uses index zero on wrap.
JSR $2F06 to make the scene visible, then jump to the saved-register restoration at $2FB8.
Apply the scene-band settings through $2F06 and continue at the main interrupt tail.
Select screen $F000 and character set $D800 via $D018=$C6. Copy scene colours from $9575/$9576 to the VIC multicolour registers, clear $6A and call the hook at $1187.
JSR $2F2B for the pocket-computer band and continue at $2FB8 to restore the saved registers.
Apply the pocket-band settings through $2F2B and continue at the main interrupt tail.
Delay by the short X countdown, then select screen $F000 and character set $D000 via $D018=$C4. Use fixed multicolours 6 and 14, signal the pocket band in $6A and wrap the tick count in $47 at $9762.
Advance the counters in $57, $4C and $47, wrap $47 at $9762 and increment $6B on the wrap. Prepare the sprite update for the index in $977A before joining the common IRQ tail.
Select byte offset zero and jump to $302D to latch collision bits and apply the first sprite band.
Select byte offset eight for the shared sprite-band writer at $302D.
Select byte offset sixteen for the shared sprite-band writer at $302D.
Select byte offset twenty-four for the shared sprite-band writer at $302D.
Jump directly to $2F8E, which inspects the saved interrupt flags before advancing the raster dispatcher.
Save A, X and Y on IRQ entry and dispatch through the writable jump at $2F8B. $2FC4 changes the two operand bytes to select the handler for the next raster event.
Low byte of the dispatch address patched by the raster scheduler from the low-byte table at $368C.
High byte of the dispatch address patched by the raster scheduler from the high-byte table at $3694.

Test the stacked B flag before scheduling the next raster line. Acknowledge VIC flags, increment the schedule index, patch the next handler and sample CIA1 port B bit 7 before selecting the common exit.
Load the next raster index from $369C, reset it from $8DE1 when a zero raster-line entry ends the schedule and patch the IRQ jump at $2F8B from the split tables at $368C and $3694.

Rotate the incoming carry into $A1CA and run the transition when its low two bits are two. Decrement an active $95C8 countdown. When it is zero on entry, set it to one, preserve $1187 across $1175 and wait with IRQs enabled until another call clears the countdown. Restore $1187 and set SID volume to $0F.

When $67 is zero and $A1D1 is clear, call $35F5, reset the stack and jump to $2C90 with interrupts enabled. When $A1D1 is set, use the interrupt return at $2FB8. With $67 set, select the ROM mapping through processor port value $35 and jump to $FE2F.

Save the sprite collision status for this band and read two sprite records from $A193 indexed by X. Prepare sprite 4 through $30AC, then write the positions of sprites 0, 1 and 4, their high X bits, and sprite pointers 0 and 1 before returning through the raster IRQ tail.

Use the selected record at $9AF1 to advance or reset its offset, combine that offset with the base X coordinate in $A193/$A194, and update sprite 4's low X, high X bit and Y in the pending band registers. A zero duration sets the pending Y to zero.
Divide the incoming band value X by eight to choose a collision slot, substituting five for zero before subtracting one. Read the VIC sprite collision latch into $A1C5 indexed by slot and restore X.
Stop CIA1 timer A, mask and acknowledge CIA1 interrupts, and enable VIC raster interrupts. Acknowledge pending VIC interrupts and clear the raster compare's high bit.
Start the common raster handover with control byte $10 and timer state $3A. It installs the IRQ at $3192 and waits for the IRQ to advance the state before drawing the scene band.

Wait for $6A, disable sprites and install raster IRQ $3192 on line $30. Initialize its state through $3119 and wait on $68 according to the sign of $69. The nonnegative path restores the scene display and sprites. The negative path sets bit six of $D011 and returns with interrupts disabled.

Save the registers and acknowledge the VIC interrupt. Below raster low byte $32, clear the two high bits of $D011 and schedule a line limited to $AB using $68. At $AC, schedule $68 and enter $2F1F. Otherwise set bit six of $D011, update $68 by $69 and schedule $30 before the IRQ return at $2FB8.
Pass $10 and $3A to the simple transition raster installer.
Set the SID voice two pulse waveform control, initialize the room's actor slots and continue into the transition raster setup.
Pass $F0 and $F8 to the simple transition raster installer.

Take the raster increment in A and start in X, install IRQ $3240, and program line $30. With a negative increment, disable sprites and wait for $68 below $32 before returning with IRQs masked. With a nonnegative increment, wait for $68 at least $F8, set the five low sprite multicolour bits and restore the display.
Write full volume to $D418 and jump to the game raster enable.

Save registers and acknowledge the VIC. Below line $32, clear the high two bits of $D011 and schedule line $68. Otherwise set bit six of $D011, schedule line $30 and add $69 to $68. Return through $2FB8.
Look up the high and low parts of forty times the row through the tables at $32A3 and $328A, add column X and return the offset at $7C/$7D.
Low bytes of forty times each row from zero through 24, indexed by Y in $3279.
High bytes paired with $328A.
Join the shared draw return at $3337 when the input row or column is beyond the 40-by-25 screen.
Save the draw option obtained from X plus one, unpack three arguments into $0E through $10 while discarding their high bytes, then restore the saved return slot and fall through to $32DE.

Reject coordinates outside a 40-by-25 character screen. Store the character at $F000 plus its row-major offset, choose a colour from the per-mode character tables when requested and write it to colour RAM. A readied clock trace stopped after the screen store at $32FB.
Save the character passed in A, set the option byte for the direct display path, and tail-call the bounds-checking writer with the supplied X and Y coordinates.
Save the character and clear the option controlling the secondary character-map copy before sharing the screen writer with $3348.
Inspect the saved processor flags. If interrupts are enabled, wait for the value at $4C to differ from the sampled value before returning.
AND the two CIA1 port reads, invert the active-low result and mask to the five direction/fire bits. Write the mask to $86B9 and $9763 and return it in the two-byte result at $0A.

Read origin and dimensions from the first four descriptor bytes at Y:X. Select the source pointer at offset 4 plus twice the variant, falling back to variant zero when A exceeds one. Read one tile per cell from the chosen source and forward it to $3348.
Set sprite zero to X $FE and Y $E4, install pointer $B8 in $F3F8 and set the sprite colours and multicolour mask. Clear the top X bit of sprites zero through four.
Set sprites zero and one to colours fifteen and one. Install pointer $B8 for sprite zero and write shared multicolour one as twelve.
Upper byte of the cursor's X position. The cursor code shifts it with the low position at $3484 and $34AC.

Apply the enable mask at $A192, wait on the raster tick, update the map marker and mission timer, then poll the sticks. When the raster tick changes, use the direction bits to move sprite zero and update its high X bit. Return the sampled input through $351F.
Copy A into the low return byte at $0A and clear X and the high return byte at $0B. Leave Y equal to one.
Reserve A bytes below software stack pointer $04/$05 and copy that many bytes from zero page $30 to the new frame. Restore the caller's Y before returning.
Restore A bytes to zero page $30 from the software stack and advance the frame pointer at $04/$05 by the same count.
XOR an indexed zero-page byte with the raster counter and the previous result at $83. Advance the zero-page index at $82, store the new result at $83 and return it at $0A while preserving X.

Use A as the fill value and X/Y as the address of a four-byte rectangle descriptor. Convert the first two bytes to a room grid address via $3279. Use the following bytes as width and height and fill the rows through $623F with a stride of $28 at $82D1.
Set border and background to black. Clear five pages starting at screen $F000 and clear all 1000 visible colour cells starting at $D800.
AND both joystick-port bytes and test bit 4 until a fire button pulls it low. The loop returns with the masked accumulator zero.
Write zero to all three SID voice control registers and return.
Set $9761 to one before entering the speech and raster delay loop at $3606.

Clear the SID voice controls, then start the record 315 speech driver at $FA87. Decrement $9B and reload it with $D3 when it reaches zero. At that point increment sprite zero's Y if $9761 is nonzero. Poll timer B through $FA98 until its running bit clears, then disable CIA2 interrupt enables, read the interrupt flags and restore the engine NMI vector.

Set all eight sprite colours to three and clear the sprite enable and X high-bit registers. Set multicolour on all sprites. Examine ten four-byte records at $A193 and skip records with byte two below eight. Use twice byte two as the offset for the two position stores. Use the running sprite number for the enable bit, the pointer store at $F3F8 and the conditional X high bit.
Low bytes of the per-event IRQ targets used by $2FC4. The first two target $2F00 and $2F25 in the elevator.
High bytes paired with $368C when $2FC4 rewrites the IRQ dispatch operand.
Index incremented in $2F8E. $2FC4 reloads it from the display mode when the next raster entry is zero.
Low raster compare values for the IRQ schedule. Zero terminates each schedule; the elevator entries are $AA and $30.
First cell in the actor band position list. $7AED sets the initial entry, $7AF2 writes a value using the actor index, and $7B30 updates it when remembering the actor's band position.
$727A compares a sprite Y value plus $17 to the threshold selected by half the sprite-record index. The band setup at $7AF7 clears the indexed threshold during initialization.
Wait for $6A to become nonzero and then zero. Reset the forward-copy operands and call the span copier twice, with $3713 adjusting the second pass.
Patch the four address operands used by the row move at $36E3. Use page $F0 and low offsets $00/$28 and $17/$3F for the two 17-byte runs.
Copy 17 bytes through two pairs of patched absolute indexed operands. After each pass increase the four base addresses by $28 and stop when the first destination low byte reaches $58.
Patched low byte of the first indexed load in the forward scroll loop. The standard setup at $36C5 writes $28.
Patched page for the first indexed load in the forward scroll loop. $36CD writes $F0.
Patched low byte for the first indexed store in the forward scroll loop. $36C0 writes zero.
Patched page for the first indexed store in the forward scroll loop. $36CA writes $F0.
Patched low byte for the second indexed load in the forward scroll loop. $36D7 writes $3F.
Patched page for the second indexed load in the forward scroll loop. $36DF writes $F0.
Patched low byte for the second indexed store in the forward scroll loop. $36D2 writes $17.
High operand byte of the second patched screen store at $36EE. The row advance updates it when its low byte crosses a page.
Patch four high operands of the forward copy to $D8.
Wait for $6A to become zero and then nonzero. Reset the backward-copy operands for each of two span copies and let $3793 alter the second pass.
Patch four pointer words in the raster handler's table references. Restore the two source tables within page $F2 and their related colour or position table pointers.
Transfer two 17-byte runs between their patched addresses. Subtract $28 from each of the four operands after a pass and stop when the first destination low byte reaches $D8.
Patched low byte of the first indexed load in the backward scroll loop. $3741 writes $08.
Patched page for the first indexed load in the backward scroll loop. $374B writes $F2.
Patched low byte for the first indexed store in the backward scroll loop. $373C writes $30.
Patched page for the first indexed store in the backward scroll loop. $3746 writes $F2.
Patched low byte for the second indexed load in the backward scroll loop. $3755 writes $1F.
Patched page for the second indexed load in the backward scroll loop. $375F writes $F2.
Patched low byte for the second indexed store in the backward scroll loop. $3750 writes $47.
High operand byte of the second screen store in the backward copier. The pointer update borrows from it when the low byte wraps.
Patch four high operands of the backward copy to $DA.

Index the five-byte resource table at $2332 with X. Transfer its destination to $89/$8A, turn the 16-bit file number into three decimal characters using $37C8 and hand control to the cassette reader at $BE00.
Copy the working file number from $0E/$0F to $12/$13. Replace the copy with remainder modulo ten, divide the working number by ten and return the remainder plus $30 as the next filename character.
Draw cassette status prompt zero, write $15 to the processor port and wait for a fire press.
For X from $D0 down to one, expose the character ROM and read $CFFF+X, then expose RAM and copy to $E1FF+X. Leave I/O visible and X equal to $4F.
Mark the transition panel active, draw it and install the ROM prompt font. Copy the selected zero-terminated message into screen cells beginning at $F1C8.
Zero-terminated REWIND string written into the screen by $3811 for the rewind prompt.
Zero-terminated WAIT string adjacent to the tape rewind message.
Eight values indexed by tower at $386B and cached in $9576 for the scene raster pass.
Eight values indexed by tower at $3865 and cached in $9575 for the scene raster pass.

Reset the current section marker, set up tower records and palette, then load the current tower's tape resource. Walk the room fields starting at offset 15; $40 skips a slot, and a populated byte contributes its low three bits to the room index table at $9C81.
Use a four-byte entry selected by the tower index. Compare the room object's type against the first and third bytes and substitute the corresponding second or fourth byte before storing it back.
First byte of each four-byte type replacement record used at $392D, selected by the tower index.
Type value selected when the first match field in the tower record succeeds.
Second input code checked by $3935 from the same four-byte records.
Second replacement code, loaded at $393A. The whole four-field record repeats for each of the eight towers before the entry at $3963.
Set all 16 bytes at $FFE0 to actor class $3F.

Double A to choose the initial slot. Walk the room actor triples starting at $82B9 and copy the two coordinates and class to the separate RAM planes at $FFC0, $FFD0 and $FFE0 when the class is $1D, $1E or $1F.
Multiply the current tower at $86BA by 16 to select the tape's first file for that tower. Patch $2337 and dispatch via the resource-table entry at offset $05.
Resolve the destination room from X, multiply the input A by $01E0 and add $A500 for its source. Copy $01A9 bytes to the room record and pass it to the unpacker at $2BCA.
A single RTS in this cassette build. A second entry one byte later starts the separate $315 resource request.
Request record 315 through table slot $23. After loading, copy twelve pages from $A520 into $F400 through $FFFF using the backward transfer at $6217.
Clear movement and display state before entering the elevator loop. Copy the two initial word values from $97AC and $9764 into their live fields, then tail-call the elevator display setup at $4068.

Read both sticks, mask input if $79 is set and dispatch separately when $8DE1 selects the room raster schedule. In the elevator, debounce fire through $73, handle the two vertical directions when both position checks pass and call the movement and rendering routines before the next input read.
Use the elevator position in $50 to look up its display position, update the lower panel through $1E88 and tail-call the elevator renderer at $28C6.
Zero the two high bytes, derive the first word from $50 and the direction sign in $4B, and derive the second from $54 plus the gap between $96 and $A3E9.
Use the sampled position at $50/$54 to locate the first room cell. Unless $70 suppresses this scan, test four cells down the column for class $1F or higher. Return the hit in carry.
Retry the second probe at $52 minus three and require it to match the first probe result in $0A. Continue with response X equal to $FA on success, or return carry clear on failure.

Test both agent bounds through $3DD2 and require them to identify the same class. Dispatch $86B9 values one, two, five/six and nine/ten to their respective platform response routines. Unhandled values return with carry clear.
Sample at Y one pixel below $53. Set carry when the returned tile class is between three and ten inclusive. Zero and the out-of-range classes return carry clear.
Increment the stored right bound at $53 to form Y and sample the room's tile plane using the current height at $50.

Sample the room tile one scanline below $53 at the side of the agent selected by the sign of $4B. Adjust X input by plus seven or minus six, preserve the returned Y in $56 and compute a character row in $55.

Require $88E9 and a starting column from $3DEF between four and $25. Test for five cells of class one, then require the next cell to be class one, two or at least $0F. Check the nearby seven columns for any class $0C through $15 within the grid. Return carry set only when all tests pass.

With $79 clear or wrapping to zero, switch scenes when the horizontal byte $50 is below $0C or at least $AC. Also branch to $3EF9 in states $0E or $1E when $53 is below $32. With a nonzero incremented $79, test $54 against $F6 and either go to $3EF9 or change the sprite display and increment $8DD2 before continuing at $3F06.
Set the horizontal position high byte to two and the low byte to $7E before entering the common room transition setup.

Set agent X to $0142 and the vertical reference to $0104. When $8DE1 is nonzero, derive the room code from $8DE2 minus $10, masked to its upper three bits, then add $11 and a further $10 when $54 is below $96. Silence all three SID voices.
Call $31E3, reset the platform records, advance the transition counter, draw the room records and tail-call the elevator state reset.
Subtract six from the low counter at $238D, adding sixty and decrementing $238C on borrow. At exhaustion clamp the counter and move the one-shot value at $3F28 into $238E.
The LDX immediate selects the counter value stored at $238E. The following instructions write zero to $3F27 and reset $238D before the room-record cleanup.

When $78 is clear, find probe offsets for the current pose $48 in the table at $3FE8. Choose offsets according to facing, read the room grid through $400D and latch tile $1E in $A331. Eligible $0C–$1C cells enter the room effect record path.
$3F68 looks for the current animation state in this list, ending the scan on the negative sentinel.
Indexed by the matching animation state from $3FE8 when the facing byte at $4B is negative. Added to the horizontal sample at $3F81.
Final byte of the negative-facing sample offsets that start in the preceding memory page.
Indexed by the matching animation state from $3FE8 when the facing byte at $4B is nonnegative. Added to the horizontal sample at $3F81.
Move X to A and rotate it through carry before entering the tile sampler.

Clamp the column from A to zero through $27 after subtracting $0C and dividing by four. From input Y, accept the $C8 rows of pixel positions starting at $32 and calculate the $28-byte-aligned cell row into $94/$95. Return the cell value in A for one through $1E, or zero for other cell classes.
Move the column in X to Y, then return zero in A. The adjacent path at $4063 returns the same result.
Return the column in Y and zero in A.

Set elevator display mode $0E in $48, copy the frame tick limit to $47 and reset the input latch, panel state and motion flags. Begin deriving the positions drawn by the panel from the mission's current location.

If $9783 is set, clear it and return carry clear. Otherwise constrain the signed vertical step in $4D to minus eight through eight, use $4261 at both sampled bounds and pass their difference to $41A5 after updating the probe through $400F. When $41A5 sets carry, zero the vertical step and return carry set if $9A3F is nonzero.
Use the sign of A and the animation state at $48 to gate entry into the contact check at $4146.

Calculate the candidate position from $54 and $4E and prepare its grid pointer through $418B. Require extent row six or greater, then scan across for the first nonzero tile below $1F. When the hit is within the 40 columns, rotate the contact flag into $4E and return carry set.
Sample the room grid with Y from $84 and save the column in $9C. Convert the two Y positions through $4261 and store their row difference in $98.
Save the candidate coordinate while sampling the room grid with $51. Store the returned column in $9C, convert the saved position through $4261 and compute the remaining horizontal extent from $52.

Check that Y is a visible column. Walk down by 40 bytes while advancing the row and consuming the count in X. Rows below six skip reading the cell. Return carry set for tile classes one through $1E, saving the residual count at $99.
Increment Y when the facing byte at $4B is nonnegative, then decrement X before returning.

Reject negative columns, adjust the scan for the current body frame and read through $94 until the column reaches $28 or the width in X expires. A cell from one to $1E takes the hit exit. A blank or a cell at least $1F advances the scan.

In states $10 through $1B, temporarily advance $94/$95 by $6D2F to the display plane and scan columns within 0 through 39. Use the sign of $4B for the initial column adjustment. Return carry set for a cell in $3F through $41 or $59 through $5B, otherwise clear, restoring the original pointer on both paths.
Subtract two from the coordinate in A through Y, then divide the resulting byte by eight to obtain the column.
Subtract twelve from A and divide the byte result by four.
Load $9D and branch to the alternate record path if it is nonzero.
Accept encoded values from three to ten, subtract three and index 18-byte platform records. Return the bytes at offsets two and fourteen through A and Y and signal an in-range value with carry clear.

Derive the current and requested limits from the agent positions. When the horizontal coordinate is below $32, apply the edge correction selected by the sign of $4B. If movement tests are enabled, run the horizontal and vertical obstacle passes and apply the signed correction at $9A.

Save A as the movement-control argument. Choose the direction from the sign of $4B and test cells along the movement of $52 in four-unit steps, limiting it where the queried room cells block the scan.
Recompute the upper and lower limits for the agent, then scan cells above and below its current position in eight-unit steps. Adjust $53 and $54 and report contacts in $A3E5 and $A3E6.
Load the remaining movement in $9B before the eight-unit upward step. The loop branch at $4499 enters at $4443 with A already loaded.
Load the remaining movement in $9B before the eight-unit downward step. The loop branch at $4530 enters at $44DB with A already loaded.

In agent states three through five or ten through twelve, derive a grid row from $53 and $54 via $3279 and the column from $9C. Use $45D5 to test two neighboring cell classes when the first test returns carry set. When both tests return carry set, save the row displacement to $8C, call $4C88 and select the horizontal correction path by the sign of $4B.
Read the tile class at ($94),Y. Return carry set for zero and for classes $1F and above, and clear for classes one through $1E.

Write $6E to the high frequency byte of SID voice 1 and fall through to a separate path when it is already zero. Otherwise subtract two from $6E and, when nonzero, from $6F, then write the latter's old value to voice 2.
Clear both SID control registers and return.

Disable the voice-three gate and increment voice one's high frequency byte up to the threshold $18 and voice two's by two up to $10. Write their envelopes and gate a sawtooth and a noise voice at volume five.
Unreferenced $60 immediately after the return at $4640 and before the five coordinate bytes. The preceding SID setup returns at $4640.
Five bytes identical to $A3E7–$A3EB, including the two intervening bytes. The initialization loop at $40A3 reads the other copy at indices zero, two and four.
Six signed deltas added to the first and second sprite Y coordinates by $4E92 and $4E9A.
$4BDE adds this frame-indexed offset to the first agent sprite's Y coordinate at $41.
$4BE6 adds this frame-indexed offset to the second agent sprite's Y coordinate at $43.
$4BEE adds this frame-indexed offset to the third agent sprite's Y coordinate at $45.
$4BF7 takes the frame-indexed horizontal offset for the coordinate at $40. It negates the offset when $4B is negative and updates the shared high bits.
$4C29 takes the frame-indexed horizontal offset for the coordinate at $44. It negates the offset when $4B is negative and updates the shared high bits.

Twenty-eight indexed pointer values used by $49B6 to select the first sprite image for the current animation frame. The update derives the other pointers from this value and enables or suppresses sprite six as needed.
First byte of a two-byte source pointer selected by twice the animation index. $49E3 copies it to the indirect pointer and patches the low address bytes of the sprite mirror instructions.
High-byte view of the same alternating low and high bytes. $49FC patches the selected page into both the indirect pointer and each absolute indexed operand.
Final three bytes of the interleaved mirror sprite source table. $49E3 reads low bytes from the base at $46A5 and $49FC reads high bytes from $46A6, both using twice the frame index.
Ending row offset for the selected frame. The mirror code reads it into Y before processing three bytes per row.
Signed offset selected by frame index at $4CA5. Add it to the base byte at $41 to get the left-side X bound checked by the room movement code.
Partner offset selected at $4CAE by the same frame index and added to the common X base to get the right-side bound.
Per-frame offsets read on two paths in the overlap helpers. The negative cases at $4CC6 are handled by using the carry of the low-byte position sum.
Partner offset table read at $4CE1 and $4D01, used with the first bound when probing a row.
Compute a 9-bit target as sprite seven's Y plus 21. Substitute raster line 255 if $79 is nonzero, then wait for the raster to drop below that target and reach it again.
Compare $D012 to the low target at $71. Convert $D011 bit 7 into the raster high bit, then subtract $72 with the carry from the low comparison. Return carry set on or above the 9-bit target.

Clear $A3E5 and dispatch separately when the motion quantity in $49 is zero. Compare it against the previous value and when the repetition count reaches two, set the signed $4D step to $08 or $F8 according to the sign of $4B.
Five starting pointer values in the agent animation sequence. $48FA reads the sequence before updating the sprite pointer group.
Call the movement routine at $4A51 and return.
Keep A when it is $0B. Otherwise add 40 to Y and read the next row from the screen pointer at $94/$95.

Clear the contact bits at $980F. Check the animation frame and $49 before probing the room grid. Sample the boundaries using $4CB7 and $4CF2, and shift the carry from each of three $41A5 probes into $980F. Return the three flags in Y.

Run $4D22 and return if $47 is set. Apply the movement routines, preserve the frame index in $76 and update the sprite registers and pointers. For frame indices $14–$19 disable sprite 6. The frame pointer at $46A5 supplies the six patched operands in the reflection pass. If the orientation byte at offset $3F already equals $4B, leave the shape unchanged.

Save the current animation index in $76 and update the sprite group coordinates. Select the base pointer through $4689 and derive the remaining pointers by adding one, with an extra step for frame indices seven through thirteen. Use the frame index to decide whether sprite six is enabled and write the resulting VIC mask.
Index the shape base table at $46A5 with twice the pose at $48. Patch the absolute operands of the mirror loop to use three consecutive byte columns at that base.
Compare byte 63 of the first sprite with the requested direction at $4B. Update the flag and reverse the pixels only when it changes.

Look up each of the three bytes through the bit-reversal table at $FCC0, writing the outer bytes into opposite columns and the middle byte back into its own column. Walk backwards by three bytes per row.
Low byte of the source address for the left sprite byte, installed at $49E8 from the frame's base pointer.
Patched high operand for the left-byte read at $4A26. The following indexed lookup at $4A29 reverses its bit order.
Low byte of the source address for the right sprite byte, installed at $49F6 from the frame's base pointer plus two.
Patched high operand for the right-byte read at $4A2C.
Low byte of the destination address for the mirrored right sprite byte. $49F9 sets it to the frame's base pointer plus two.
Patched high operand for the write of the mirrored left byte into the right column at $4A2F.
Low byte of the destination address for the mirrored left sprite byte, installed at $49EB from the frame's base pointer.
Patched high operand for writing the mirrored right byte to the left column at $4A35.
Low byte of the source address for the middle sprite byte. $49EF sets it to the frame's base pointer plus one.
Patched high operand for the middle-byte read at $4A38.
Low byte of the destination address for the mirrored middle sprite byte. $49F2 sets it to the frame's base pointer plus one.
Patched high operand of the store at $4A3E. The following loop steps Y back three bytes per row and skips the stride byte at each sprite boundary.

Add pending deltas at $4D and $4E to the three coordinate pairs at $40–$45. Write their low X and Y minus four to VIC sprites 5–7. Fold X carries into the saved high bits at $46, write them to $D010, then clear both deltas. Recompute the bounds in $51–$54 and the midpoints in $4F–$50. A right bound of at least $F8 increments $79 and clears $86B9.

For eligible frames, use $86B9 or the existing orientation at $4B to choose a direction and horizontal motion. If the new direction changes $4B, reset the frame to $0E and derive a corrective delta from the room grid. That exit discards the caller's return address and resumes the update at $49AA.
Patched immediate operand of ADC at $4B67. The following subtraction and shift derive the horizontal sprite delta in $4D.
$4B3F saves A after rotating in the result of the overlap check. The frame displacement calculation subtracts it at $4B6A.

Advance the countdown in $48. A pending $75 request during frames below $10 clears that request, writes $80 to SID voice 3 control and selects frame $1B. The later range counts down to $0E, or to $0D when either of bits 2 and 3 at $86B9 is set.

For pose values below $10 apply the same low X delta at $88 to the three pairs at $40, $42 and $44 and update the high bits in $46. For later poses select per-sprite vertical and horizontal offsets from the tables beginning at $464D.
Negate A into $8C and add it to each of the three position low bytes at $40, $42 and $44. Pack the carries and use them to update the position high bits in $46.
Store A as the vertical delta at $8C and jump to the group update at $4C5A.
Subtract $8C from each of the three vertical sprite coordinates at $41, $43 and $45.
Add Y to each of the three vertical sprite coordinates at $41, $43 and $45.
Read the frame offset at $470B and add it to $41.
Read the frame offset at $472D and add it to the same base.
Load Y with the animation frame at $48 before testing vertical overlap.

Use the direction flag in $4B and index Y to choose the row boundary from $474F or $4771. Combine it with $40 and return the overlap decision in carry. The extent mode in bit five of $46 is used when the addition does not establish the result directly.
Load the agent Y byte from $48 before entering the common vertical overlap test at $4CF2.

Start with the extent bit from $46 and choose the boundary at $4771 or its alternate at $474F using the sign of $4B. Add the current offset $40 and return either the extent bit or a set carry when the position sum overflows.
Return when the motion flag $79 is set. Frames zero, seven and $10 start a voice-three effect, while frames $03, $0A, $0E and $1C or above write $80 to its control register.
Set full SID volume, choose one of two frequency words from the sign of $4B, then set voice three's ADSR and enable its noise waveform with gate.
Three pointer bytes used when the opening elevator installs idle agent sprites at $F3FD–$F3FF.
Three colour bytes installed for sprites 5–7 alongside the idle pointers.
Copy the idle pointer and colour for sprites five through seven to the VIC state and clear the corresponding three multicolour bits.
The side-cell check saves the probe result at $4E30 or $4E41. The path at $4E44 tests the saved value against $1E.
Require horizontal position from $10 through $A9 and zero in $78, $79 and $49. Only then enter the idle pose contact routine.
Derive the probe origin from the agent coordinates. The pose at $48 chooses two offsets for $4E55 to sample. Update $4D94 with the first applicable result and write $A331 when the sample code is $1E.
Select the offset from X or Y according to the sign of $4B. Add it to the horizontal probe origin at $8E/$8F, convert to a column and tail-call $400D with the row at $90.

Set the voice-three control to $80 and patch the mirrored sprite positions. Normalize the animation byte $48 when it reaches $21. The table at $4EA2 provides the first of three consecutive pointers for sprites six, seven and five. Apply the matched delta at $4647 to both coordinates before moving the group.
First VIC pointer for each frame selected by $4E81. The first three are $D0, $D3 and $D6, which select the three slot groups beginning at $F400, $F4C0 and $F580 in bank $C000.
Four pairs of tile IDs. $5031 reads the entry selected by twice the tile class plus the low horizontal phase bit.
Four tile values used by $584C and $5853 when restoring the visible portion of a room object.
Tile codes read by the room-object update at $5830 or selected as a fallback at $585B. The latter path uses the running tile index at $88.
Seven low bytes of the pointers to room draw counts. $4F3F loads one for each draw dispatch.
Seven corresponding high bytes loaded by $4F44.
Seven low bytes of the room drawing calls. The high bytes at $4EE1 pair by index. $4F56 and $4F5C fetch the pair before $4F71 calls it.
Seven high bytes paired with $4EDA, in the same order as the count and record pointers in the room drawing loop.
Low bytes of the working draw-argument pointers, indexed by the record class at $4F62.
High bytes of the working draw-argument pointers read at $4F67.
Sizes of the room draw arguments. $5018 uses the size as the copy count and $4F76 uses it to advance the source after a draw.

Relocate the seven count and record pointers against room buffer $7FD3 on the first call. For each nonempty list, patch the call at $4F71, unpack each record into $94 onward, call the indexed drawing routine, then advance by that list's record stride at $4EF6.

Clear the room and initialize its platform records. Relocate two sets of seven split pointers by $7FD3 when the first high byte is zero. For each nonempty group, set the item count in the compare operand at $4F83 and patch the draw call at $4F71 from the group's routine pointer. Process each record, stepping its pointer by the group's size from $4EF6.
$4F59 patches this byte with the indexed target low byte. The companion operand at $4F73 supplies the target page for the call at $4F71.
High byte of the patched JSR at $4F71, selected at $4F5C. After the draw, advance the parameter stream by the selected record size and repeat until the record count is reached.

Mutable immediate operand of the CMP at $4F82. The group loader writes its count here at $4F4F. The continuation advances to the next group. After the last group it either reruns after $5F2A or initializes room effects and actors and restores the display.

Choose column zero or $27 from agent X high byte and row three or $17 from $8DE0. Step down that column in $28-byte increments until seeing tile class one, two or $0B, or until the eight-bit offset returns to zero. Convert the resulting row to a coordinate and write it to $8DDF/$8DE0 and $97AC/$97AD.
Copy the record at ($86) into $94 onward, taking the byte count from the stride table at $4EF6 indexed by X. Zero length skips the copy.
Enter with the byte count in Y and copy that many bytes from ($86) to ($94), working backwards.
Index $4EA8 by twice A plus the parity of X. Preserve Y in $8C and return the selected tile in A.
Index $4EA8 by twice A plus the parity of Y. Preserve X in $8C and return the selected tile in A.
Convert coordinates through the shared screen offset routine and add its 16-bit byte offset to the destination pointer at $80.
Set the destination base to $82D1 and add the offset for the column and row at $94 and $95.
Address the $0340 grid at column $94 and row $95 minus one. Return the tiles 40 cells apart in $8A and $8B. At the top boundary, use $FF for the preceding tile and read the first row into $8B.
