Initialize the destination pointer to the room grid at $4003. Add the offset $99 to the row or column according to $96, then use the grid pointer helper for a nonnegative preceding row. The negative-row path instead returns a pointer in page three.

Select $D018=$C8, apply the appropriate palette and clear the 1,000-byte auxiliary room grid at $82D1. Fill all 40 by 25 screen cells through $334E with tile zero when $8DC5 is set, and tile three otherwise.

Select a four-byte shape descriptor through $AFB6 using $96, with a special descriptor at $AFAE for types two or three when $8DC5 is set. Read the descriptor's dimensions and source pointer, then unpack tiles, clip their coordinates to the visible screen and mark the auxiliary plane for the cells drawn.

Use $94 as the column, $95 as the first row and $96 as the height. Write $0B to each corresponding cell in the $D182 auxiliary plane. Draw alternating tiles in the strip, with edge tiles above it and on its right where the coordinates permit.
Mark $96 consecutive cells in the $D182 plane as type one. Read the nearby $0340 cells, then choose the screen tiles and caps from those neighbours and the strip position.
Mark $96 consecutive cells in the $D182 plane as type two. Use the tiles returned in $8A and $8B and the row and column coordinates to select strip and boundary tiles.
Start at column $94 plus one and row $95 plus $97 minus two. Offset the horizontal run as successive rows are drawn and select boundary tiles from adjoining grid cells.
Use the fields at $96 and $99 through $9D to choose a row and column in the $0340 plane and place matching tiles on the screen. The $96 zero case takes the separate horizontal path at $5542.

Loop over $98 rows, using $94 and $95 for each origin. When $96 is nonzero, copy four adjacent tiles with a source and destination row choice controlled by $A2. Otherwise draw the pair from offsets 0 and $28 in column zero for selector eight, or offsets 3 and $2B in column three. Clear three cells in the runtime grid for rows below 25 before advancing to the next record row.
Zero immediate operand of the LDA at $55A9. The cap-row loop starts with this value in A, then puts it in $88 at $55AB.
Read the tiles adjacent to the record's origin and use their codes to choose the four parts of the screen group. Two calls to $5037 use the row parity to select a tile variant.
Second of two INX instructions that move the draw column two right of $94. The following DEY selects the row above $95 before $3348 writes tile five.

Index a four-byte record from $7FD7 by A, copy it to $94 onward and derive its auxiliary-plane pointer. Draw a four-tile cap from $4EB4 and use the fourth field and nearby room-cell classes to decide the additional tile and shape writes.
Low byte of the indexed load at $583F. The captured instruction addresses $0340 before adding Y.

High operand of the indexed load at $583F. $581C writes it from the row address returned by $5047. The following path draws the cap tiles, handles the associated object through $7024 and clears the corresponding auxiliary cell.

Save object column, row and class from X, Y and A. Return if $7FD6 exceeds the class-dependent limit of eight or nine. Write the object number plus $0C into the room cell returned by $5058 and append those fields and the $3E/$3F selector to the four-byte object table at $7FD7. Clear $88E9 and draw the marker one row above via $5B30.
Look up the current room index via $88E8, fetch its kind from $9C81 and apply the three corresponding table entries to $D021–$D023.
Zero the preview selector at $7FD2 and VIC background colour before jumping to $5884.

Set VIC colours to 0, 1 and 3. Back up the $82D1 cell plane at $E000, the $0340 tile grid at $E3C0 and $F0 glyph bytes from $9B36 at $C38C. Copy the replacement tile range from $A220 to $E000 and a matching block from $E000 to $E800. Install $1D bytes at $C38C from $A203 and three glyphs at $E768 from $A11C.
Restore the room palette through $58F3. Copy the saved planes from $E000 to $82D1 and from $E3C0 to $0340. Restore $F0 bytes from the backup at $C38C to $9B36 and leave through $5884.
Copy the fixed checker glyph into $E780, then choose either a fifteen-entry glyph list or the later small-list path based on the supplied layout number.
For each of fifteen glyph IDs select a colour at $9CCD and an eight-byte shape at $9D54. Pack the shapes consecutively at $E788 and the colours at $8DB4.

Multiply each tile index read through $12 by eight and add the page supplied in X to the character source. Copy the resulting eight rows through $80 and move the destination ahead by eight. Increment $16 and stop at two or four.
Shift two chains of three eight-byte glyphs left by four bits per row. Then copy four-byte half-glyphs into the preceding columns, clearing the last half at the end of each row group.
Multiply the glyph code by eight and return the resulting pointer relative to $E000, with its low byte in Y and high byte in X.
Set to $FF at $4EFF before the cache setup. $5B49 increments this index before selecting a slot code from $5BD5.
$5B4F indexes this sequence after incrementing the room glyph allocation slot. The selected tile code supplies the destination glyph at $5B54.
Compute the platform record offset through $5BF1, then copy its 18 bytes from $80FF plus that offset to the working array at $94.
Store the record index in $8C and compute eighteen times that index in A and X. Store the offset in $84.
Require X and Y in the 40-by-25 room grid, point $80 at that cell through $5047 and return carry set for classes one through $1E. Coordinates outside the grid return carry clear.
Begin at $80FF and visit $80FE records of stride $12. Clear offsets $0F through $11 in each record.

Walk $80FE records of $12 bytes at $80FF. Copy field six into field three, clear field $0E and restore the two live coordinates from $5CB4 in field order determined by field two. Also restore fields zero and four of $80AA from fields three and seven respectively.
Return field eight of the current record in A and the byte indexed by field six plus nine in X. The record pointer is $86/$87.

When $A2 is clear, test for platform class one with field $97 set and run the coordinate test through $5BFD. On success add $9783 to $4D. The successful path and the direct $A2 path store their result in the current platform's active field at $810D plus $84.

Branch out when the alternate-order flag $A2 is set. For the eligible mode, compare the candidate offset and test the target row and column with $5BFD. Select step code two for the pass through $5CFC when the tile test returns carry clear.

Check that the active mode and candidate offset permit a horizontal move. Call the room-cell test for the candidate column and $9C row. On clear carry return through the step dispatcher with mask four.

Require a horizontal platform and an eligible candidate offset. Calculate its target column through the scratch array and call $5BFD with the candidate row. A clear carry selects step mask eight before returning to the platform pass.

Skip while $A396 is nonzero. Add eight to $4E when $79 is nonzero and $49 is zero. Clear $57 and the active count at $8919, then scan $80FE records from $80FF with stride $12. For each with field $0E set, increment the active count and update through $5BDF and $5DED. Clear fields $0F through $11 of each visited record.

Erase the old platform tiles, then use the mode at $A2 to change coordinates in the record selected by $84. Redraw the platform and update the carried agent coordinate and attached slots where their flags are set.
Decrement X, then subtract eight from the word starting at $7079 plus X, borrowing into its high byte.
Decrement X, then add eight to the word starting at $7079 plus X, carrying into its high byte.
Decrement X, then subtract eight from the word starting at $7077 plus X, borrowing into its high byte.
Decrement X, then add eight to the word starting at $7077 plus X, carrying into its high byte.

Select one of two records by choosing index zero or four. Probe the tile immediately before the start and then the tile at the far end through $5BFD. Use those carry results to decide whether to decrement the start column toward zero or increment it toward $27.
Read the start column and row from the selected record and tail-call $5BFD with X one cell left of that column.
Add the width field to the start column and tail-call $5BFD with that column and the saved row.

Set the current platform index in $85, clear $9783 and set $9C62. After $5BDF, pick the pair of update tests from $96. Use the low bit of the result from $3561 to order the pair. Skip the second test if the first leaves Z clear.

Reset the dynamic glyph destination and shape ID cache, and clear the 300-byte allocation workspace at $9B36. Choose the alternate shape descriptor when $8DC5 is set. Otherwise walk the room's five-byte shape records and use $604C to allocate tiles for their descriptors.

Return success early if A already occurs in the shape cache. Otherwise load the four-byte descriptor at $AFB6 plus four times A. Temporarily put the allocation workspace at $0340, unpack the tile stream to count its zero entries, then move the workspace back to $9B36. Allocate only if the resulting glyph range fits below $F1.

Write the current dynamic glyph number into the allocation cell at ($1A) and advance it. Copy an eight-byte shape from the resource beginning at $A520, add its colour to the room colour table and restore the decoder index from the patched operand at $61A9.

Read the next index through $18 and combine it with a packed high bit from $1C using the mask table at $61AB. Build the pointer for the corresponding allocation at $9B36, advance the packed bit cursor, read the allocation byte and return with Y advanced to the next index.
Saved Y while looking up a room glyph allocation and flag. $6172 writes it and $61A3 restores it for the caller.
Glyph allocation scan index. $6179 loads it, and $618A advances it to the next candidate.
One descending bit per glyph within an allocation byte, indexed at $617C.

Save the low three bits of the glyph index in the mask operand at $61AA. Add $B0A6 to the full index for the glyph allocation pointer. Divide a saved copy of the index by eight and add $B394 for the packed flag lookup.
Add A to the word at zero-page offset X, storing the low byte and incrementing the high byte on carry.
Subtract A from the word at zero-page offset X by negating the low result of A minus the low byte. Decrement the high byte when A exceeds the old low byte.
Set the source pointer $7E/$7F from Y:X for the indexed copy routines.
Set the destination pointer $80/$81 from Y:X for the copy and fill routines.
Copy Y bytes from ($7E) to ($80) in descending index order, ending with index zero. Callers supply a nonzero count.
Copy X full pages plus Y additional bytes, working backward through indexed source and destination pointers. Y zero starts from the previous full page. Both pointers' high bytes are updated in place.
Write the input A into Y bytes at ($80) in descending index order, ending with index zero. A is unchanged.
Fill X full pages plus Y bytes with the supplied A. The loop uses the high byte of the destination pointer as a descending page counter.

Decrement $8CC2 and return while it is nonzero. Otherwise update the sprite enable mask and scan four bytes at $A1C5. For each with any high-three bit set, take the low five bits as the index at $6304 and add its byte to $62AF for the indirect jump through $12/$13.
Continue scanning the command bytes at $62A4.

When the command index in Y differs from $9597, XOR it with $0F and combine it with the high three sprite-enable bits. Remember the index and increment $9814. When the index matches, increment $9598 and clear both fields when it reaches five.
If $9779 is set, call $6324 and continue at $3F03. Otherwise resume the band command scan.
Use twice X as the index at $A1BB, then test the byte at $7082 indexed by the result. Go to $62E0 when it is below $1D and otherwise continue the scan.
Use twice X plus one as the index at $A1BB and share the class test at $62F1.

Thirty-two unsigned offsets from $62AF for the low five bits of each command. Indices one and two test even and odd actor slots. Index $10 enters the threshold handler. Indices $11 through $1F share the sprite mask handler. The remaining indices resume the scan.
Supply zero to the common dissolve entry. The BIT at $6326 consumes the alternate entry's LDA immediate instruction so this path retains A equal to zero.

Set $A3EC, increment $8DD2 and prepare the effect at $63A2. Repeatedly mask bytes in the three sprite buffers $F640, $F680 and $F6C0 with values from $6454. End by zeroing all three buffers, writing $08 to SID voices 2 and 3 control, and setting $8CC2 to six.

Walk sprite pointers seven through five, multiply each by 64 and add the VIC bank base $C000. Copy all 64 bytes into the three consecutive slots beginning at $F640, then replace each pointer with one in the $D9 to $DB group.

Call the wait routine at $335F and start the dissolve sound. Set sprites six and seven to a colour indexed by X, then wait and replace it with the alternate table value. When $A3EC is zero, apply the opposite colour to sprite five in both phases.
Two zero colour bytes used by the alternating writes at $63E3 and $6408.
Colours eleven and twelve used by the alternating writes at $63F1 and $63FA.
Skip when the sign bit of $78 is set. Initialize SID voices two and three with pulse and noise waveforms and their envelopes, then use the low three bits returned by $3561 as the SID volume.
Use the low three bits of a random value to pick a byte mask and the low six bits of a second value to set the byte offset in X. Return the mask in A.
Eight masks with one cleared bit each. The dissolve selector at $645A reads one before choosing a sprite-byte offset.

Return immediately when $A396 is zero. Otherwise select the active shape at $8DD4, set the colour override for the room palette and draw the region using the active record at $A399 and its bitmap descriptor near $AFB6.

Save object tile ID in $8DD4 and play effect three. Subtract $1F from the ID to find its five-byte object record at $80B3. Types two and three take the separate path through $68E6 and $692F. For the timed path require nonzero type and countdown, compute a bounded display origin from the shape descriptor near $AFB6, then save the record pointer and pending reward in $A399 and $A398.

Require active search $A396 and bit zero of $4C. Decrement byte three of the active record and redraw the remaining meter. At zero, process the pending $A398 reward, with effects that include clock adjustment and counter increments, then clear the pending reward.
Increment the byte of the selected search overlay triplet. The preceding calculation patches both address bytes of this instruction.
The low byte of the search overlay triplet address is set at $666A from the shape number scaled by three.

High address byte of the patched increment instruction at $6674. Rewards zero through six select a counter near $88D2 with stride three. After the increment or branch past it, $6677 checks the reward code and applies the associated timer or counter effect.
Three selector bytes, five, seven and three. The branch at $66CA bounds the decimal tens digit in Y below three before $66CF uses it to select the replacement for $7FD2.

Set $7FD2 to $FE, and for eligible reward IDs use $1088 and $66B6 to select a different drawing mode. Call $59E2 with the resulting selector and draw descending temporary tile codes from $877D in the rectangle based on $A397 and $A39D. Some paths finish by painting the lower row with tile $FE.
Shift an all-ones mask left according to the input A, apply it to each of the eight bytes at $E7F8 and save the masked glyph at $E7E8. Restore X and Y before returning.
Run the cached cell restore only while $A396 indicates an active overlay. Clear it before tail-calling the restore path.

Add the column $A397 to 32 times row $A39D plus the low byte of eight times that row. Save the corresponding $D800 and $F000 plane pointers in $963D through $9640. Cache five rows of seven bytes from each plane consecutively at $A39E, with the $F000 plane first.
Add 40 to the zero-page pointer selected by X through $61E4.
Add five to the zero-page pointer selected by X. The caller at $6CD7 uses X equal to $14 to move to the next five-byte source row after copying three bytes.
Advance destination pointer $0E/$0F by seven bytes with carry for the next cached row.
Copy ten rows of seven bytes beginning at $A39E. The first five rows go to the pointer read at $963D and the other five to the pointer at $963F. Both destinations use row stride forty.
Set the display parameter at $877D, call $66B9 and then draw the outline and side tiles of the active overlay using its origin in $A397/$A39D.
Offsets zero, 25 and 50 from $86BB. The decimal tens digit of the piece number selects the record at $6889.
Ignore values of at least $1E. Convert the value through $1088, choose one of the three records at $86BB using the quotient and append the remainder after the count if the count is below $14.

Remove the caller return address and patch it into the dispatch operands. Save $30 through $30 plus X and the count on the stack. Push a return address for $68C9 and the patched dispatch target, then transfer through RTS.
The high return-address byte popped by $68AE is installed in this immediate operand. The dispatcher pushes it immediately before the corresponding low byte.
The low return-address byte popped by $68AA is installed in this immediate operand. The RTS uses the pair to continue in the caller with the scratch bytes stacked.
Set the panel colour from $8DC5, pull the saved count and restore the bytes into zero page at $30. Rejoin the return at $68E2.
Set X to zero and take the return path at $68E2.
Compute the address and mask via $68F8, OR in the mask and write the changed byte through $7E.
Compute the object address and mask via $68F8 and return their AND in A. Zero means that bit is clear.

Use A's low three bits for the object's bit mask. Build a byte offset from 12 times the tower and twice the room index, plus one when A is at least eight. Add the offset to $95DD and load the flags byte, leaving the mask at $80.

In the final area with the position check below $10, dispatch to the ending when the selected record's fifth byte is three. Other values run the failure path and increment $A3E4. Outside that branch, open the six-action selector, poll horizontal stick input and dispatch on fire, spending a charge only when the selected inventory count is nonzero.

Skip action zero and empty inventory slots. Otherwise decrement the count in the three-byte command record at $88D0 plus three times the selected action. Apply the selected action, then refresh the sprites, palette and room drawing.
Set the preview selector at $7FD2 to one, draw the current choice and reset the selector to $FF.
Set the preview selector at $7FD2 to seven, draw the current choice and reset the selector to $FF.
If the search index $7FB2 is nonzero, triple it and select that offset into the records at $88D0 for the paired glyph display. Index zero takes the alternate draw path at $6D5B.

Select the display setup from $8DE1, then draw the panel frame with repeated character rectangles. Before a restart, $A1F3 selects seven four-column strips with successive colours. The other path reads three-byte entries backwards from $88E2.

Read the screen position and encoded value through $34, then split the value via $1088. Draw the first three-by-three symbol if the high component is nonzero, and draw the second three columns to the right.
Use nine times the supplied symbol index plus the glyph base near $7A, and draw three consecutive tiles per row for three rows. Restore the column after drawing each row.
Save the column and row one cell before the supplied X and Y. Derive a tile offset from the result selector in A and transfer to the overlay replacement routine with A set to one.
Load selectors one through six through $59E2 and store their results through $6CEA. Repeat for selectors $09–$12 with the alternate cache routine $6C72.

Use the selector in A to choose a destination at $E148 plus $48 times the selector. Copy four rows of $18 bytes from $E790 onward, stepping the source by $28. Copy a three-byte row from the secondary plane at $8DB5 alongside each row, stepping the secondary source by five.
Use A minus one as the shape index. Copy $78 bytes from $E788 to a slot at $E100 plus $78 times that index. Copy $0F bytes from $8DB4 to the corresponding slot at $8CE3 with stride $0F.
Add the supplied width and height to X and Y to form exclusive bounds. Use $3348 to fill the rectangle with the character in A and restart at the saved X for each row.
Call the two-wait helper three times and fall through for a fourth pair.
Call the raster-progress wait once, then tail-call it again.
Load the current tower record and clear bit seven in the six bytes at offsets three through eight.
Five two-byte entries loaded by $6F5E and $6F64. The index comes from the frame-offset table at $7FCA.

Write eight to the sixteen VIC sprite coordinate registers and the shared X high-bit register in descending address order.
Zero byte immediately past the eight 20-byte actor slots. A sentinel here survived the VICE watch at the end of their initialization loop, which stops at $7116.

Fetch the X-indexed low and high update addresses and store them in actor record offsets nine and ten.

Subtract one from the byte at offset Y in the actor record pointed to by $30/$31.

Seed $9A92 with $0E before the sound entry updates the pulse width.

Index changed by the console input loop. $69C0 tests it for zero and the following arithmetic multiplies a nonzero selection by three.

Index into the offset list at $7FCA for the alternate room effect.
Index into the six-value room effect sequence at $7FB6. $6FE5 advances it and $6FF1 resets it.

Byte offsets into the pointer list at $6D9F, selected by the effect frame at $7FB4.

Last field of the seventh three-byte actor record, from offset eighteen into the indexed class stores at $7D87 and $7DB7.

Row for the same actor entry. $7DB0 stores the result of subtracting $C8 and dividing the actor Y by eight.

Positive joystick mask written at $3376 by the two-port poll. The elevator reads it at $3A4F and $3A85.

Two-column by six-row rectangle at column 22, row five. Its graphics are $8E00 and $8E0C for the two draw modes.
Four copies of a four-pointer list selecting consecutive 17-character rows $90B0, $90C1, $90D2 and $90E3. The left and right quarter lookup branches can select this table.

Second return-address byte pulled at engine entry and saved at $2D97.

Eight values for $D022, indexed by the same room kind.
Eight values for $D023, loaded in the final colour store of $58F3.

Cleared at $6EA7 on a new room effect phase and advanced at $6EEC while processing effects.
